claim: CIDE-N domains mediate interactions between the DNase Dff40/CAD and its inhibitor Dff45/ICAD.
source: CIDE-N domains mediate interactions between the DNase Dff40/CAD and its inhibitor Dff45/ICAD.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citation to established literature.

claim: Drep-2 is a novel synaptic protein important for learning and behavioral adaptation.
source: In this study, we report that the CIDE-N protein Drep-2 is a novel synaptic protein important for learning and behavioral adaptation.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Drep-2 was found at synapses throughout the Drosophila brain.
source: Drep-2 was found at synapses throughout the Drosophila brain and was strongly enriched at mushroom body input synapses.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Drep-2 was strongly enriched at mushroom body input synapses.
source: Drep-2 was found at synapses throughout the Drosophila brain and was strongly enriched at mushroom body input synapses.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: Drep-2 was required within Kenyon cells for normal olfactory short- and intermediate-term memory.
source: It was required within Kenyon cells for normal olfactory short- and intermediate-term memory.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Drep-2 colocalized with metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluRs).
source: Drep-2 colocalized with metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluRs).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Chronic pharmacological stimulation of mGluRs compensated for drep-2 learning deficits.
source: Chronic pharmacological stimulation of mGluRs compensated for drep-2 learning deficits, and drep-2 and mGluR learning phenotypes behaved non-additively, suggesting that Drep 2 might be involved in effective mGluR signaling.
evidence: This is supported by pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 6C.

claim: drep-2 and mGluR learning phenotypes behaved non-additively.
source: Chronic pharmacological stimulation of mGluRs compensated for drep-2 learning deficits, and drep-2 and mGluR learning phenotypes behaved non-additively, suggesting that Drep 2 might be involved in effective mGluR signaling.
evidence: This is supported by double mutant analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Drep-2 might be involved in effective mGluR signaling.
source: Chronic pharmacological stimulation of mGluRs compensated for drep-2 learning deficits, and drep-2 and mGluR learning phenotypes behaved non-additively, suggesting that Drep 2 might be involved in effective mGluR signaling.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the non-additive phenotypes and pharmacological rescue.

claim: Drosophila fragile X protein mutants benefit from attenuation of mGluR signaling.
source: In fact, Drosophila fragile X protein mutants, shown to benefit from attenuation of mGluR signaling, profited from the elimination of drep-2.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work and by the double mutant data in Figure 6E.

claim: Drosophila fragile X protein mutants profited from the elimination of drep-2.
source: In fact, Drosophila fragile X protein mutants, shown to benefit from attenuation of mGluR signaling, profited from the elimination of drep-2.
evidence: This is supported by double mutant analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Drep-2 is a novel regulatory synaptic factor, probably intersecting with metabotropic signaling and translational regulation.
source: Thus, Drep-2 is a novel regulatory synaptic factor, probably intersecting with metabotropic signaling and translational regulation.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the genetic interactions and mass spectrometry data.

claim: Dff40/CAD degrades DNA during apoptosis.
source: One of their targets is the DNase Dff40/CAD, which degrades DNA during apoptosis (Enari et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Enari et al., 1998.

claim: Dff40 is a member of the DNA fragmentation factor (Dff) family of proteins.
source: Dff40 is a member of the DNA fragmentation factor (Dff) family of proteins, characterized by CIDE-N domains that mediate protein–protein interactions (Wu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wu et al., 2008.

claim: CIDE-N domains mediate protein–protein interactions.
source: Dff40 is a member of the DNA fragmentation factor (Dff) family of proteins, characterized by CIDE-N domains that mediate protein–protein interactions (Wu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wu et al., 2008.

claim: Four CIDE-N domain proteins were identified in Drosophila and named Dff related protein Drep-1 to Drep-4.
source: In Drosophila, four CIDE-N domain proteins were identified and named Dff related protein Drep-1 to Drep-4 (Inohara and Nuñez, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Inohara and Nuñez, 1999.

claim: Drep-4 is the ortholog of mammalian Dff40/CAD.
source: Caspase-regulated Drep-4 is the ortholog of mammalian Dff40/CAD (Yokoyama et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yokoyama et al., 2000.

claim: Drep-4 is inhibited by Drep-1.
source: Drep-4 is inhibited by Drep-1, the ortholog of Dff45/ICAD, which is also cleaved by caspases (Mukae et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mukae et al., 2000.

claim: Drep-1 is the ortholog of Dff45/ICAD.
source: Drep-4 is inhibited by Drep-1, the ortholog of Dff45/ICAD, which is also cleaved by caspases (Mukae et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mukae et al., 2000.

claim: Drep-1 is cleaved by caspases.
source: Drep-4 is inhibited by Drep-1, the ortholog of Dff45/ICAD, which is also cleaved by caspases (Mukae et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mukae et al., 2000.

claim: Drep-2 and -3 were suggested to be additional regulators of apoptosis, solely based on in vitro interactions.
source: The two other Drosophila family members, Drep-2 and -3, were suggested to be additional regulators of apoptosis, solely based on in vitro interactions (Inohara and Nuñez, 1999; Park and Park, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Inohara and Nuñez, 1999 and Park and Park, 2012.

claim: drep-2 mutants display learning and memory deficits.
source: We have generated drep-2 mutants, which display learning and memory deficits.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Drep-2 regulates learning and memory processes by intersecting with metabotropic glutamate receptor signaling.
source: Further analyses suggest that Drep-2 regulates these processes by intersecting with metabotropic glutamate receptor signaling.
evidence: This is an inference based on genetic and pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Both Drep-4 and Drep-2 are controlled by caspase-mediated cleavage of their inhibitors Drep-1 and Drep-3, respectively.
source: Both proteins are controlled by caspase-mediated cleavage of their inhibitors Drep-1 and Drep-3, respectively (Mukae et al., 2000; Park and Park, 2012, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mukae et al., 2000 and Park and Park, 2012, 2013.

claim: The roles of Drep-4 and -1 during apoptosis have been firmly established.
source: The roles of Drep-4 and -1 during apoptosis have been firmly established, yet the functions of Drep-2 and -3 have so far remained unknown (Inohara and Nuñez, 1999; Park and Park, 2012; Tan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Inohara and Nuñez, 1999; Park and Park, 2012; Tan et al., 2012.

claim: The functions of Drep-2 and -3 have so far remained unknown.
source: The roles of Drep-4 and -1 during apoptosis have been firmly established, yet the functions of Drep-2 and -3 have so far remained unknown (Inohara and Nuñez, 1999; Park and Park, 2012; Tan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Inohara and Nuñez, 1999; Park and Park, 2012; Tan et al., 2012.

claim: The gene coding for Drep-2 is located on chromosome IIR and contains five exons.
source: The gene coding for Drep-2 is located on chromosome IIR and contains five exons (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The last two exons of drep-2 are used in all known isoforms.
source: While the last two exons are used in all known isoforms, the first three exons are included alternatively within the four isoforms drep-2-RA to -RD.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The first three exons of drep-2 are included alternatively within the four isoforms drep-2-RA to -RD.
source: While the last two exons are used in all known isoforms, the first three exons are included alternatively within the four isoforms drep-2-RA to -RD.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: High-throughput RT-PCR data indicate a strong enrichment of both drep-2-RA and drep-3 transcripts in the central nervous system (CNS).
source: High-throughput RT-PCR data indicate a strong enrichment of both drep-2-RA and drep-3 transcripts in the central nervous system (CNS), while drep-4 and -1 are expressed ubiquitously (Graveley et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Graveley et al., 2011.

claim: drep-4 and -1 are expressed ubiquitously.
source: High-throughput RT-PCR data indicate a strong enrichment of both drep-2-RA and drep-3 transcripts in the central nervous system (CNS), while drep-4 and -1 are expressed ubiquitously (Graveley et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Graveley et al., 2011.

claim: In situ hybridization confirmed that the expression of drep-2 is nervous system specific.
source: We conducted in situ hybridization using drep-2-RA constructs in order to confirm that the expression of drep-2 is nervous system specific (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Western blots from wild-type fly head extracts probed with Drep-2C-Term showed a double band of the size expected for Drep-2 isoforms.
source: Western blots from wild-type fly head extracts probed with Drep-2C-Term showed a double band (Figure 1C) of the size expected for Drep-2 isoforms (McQuilton et al., 2012).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C and supported by citation to McQuilton et al., 2012.

claim: All drep-2 exons are deleted in homozygous drep-2ex13 animals.
source: All drep-2 exons are deleted in homozygous drep-2ex13 animals, while no other annotated transcription unit is affected.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: No other annotated transcription unit is affected in drep-2ex13 mutants.
source: All drep-2 exons are deleted in homozygous drep-2ex13 animals, while no other annotated transcription unit is affected.
evidence: This is stated in the text.

claim: In drep-2ex27, all drep-2 exons apart from the very small (12 bp) first exon are eliminated.
source: In the smaller intragenic deletion drep-2ex27, all drep-2 exons apart from the very small (12 bp) first exon are eliminated.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Both Drep-2C-Term antibody bands were absent in head extracts of both drep-2ex13 and drep-2ex27 mutants.
source: Both Drep-2C-Term antibody bands were absent in head extracts of both mutants (Figure 1C), confirming the complete elimination of Drep-2 expression in these deletion alleles.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The absence of Drep-2C-Term antibody bands confirms the complete elimination of Drep-2 expression in drep-2ex13 and drep-2ex27 deletion alleles.
source: Both Drep-2C-Term antibody bands were absent in head extracts of both mutants (Figure 1C), confirming the complete elimination of Drep-2 expression in these deletion alleles.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Western blot data in Figure 1C.

claim: Flies lacking drep-2 were viable and fertile.
source: Flies lacking drep-2 were viable and fertile but shorter-lived than the isogenic controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text.

claim: Flies lacking drep-2 were shorter-lived than the isogenic controls.
source: Flies lacking drep-2 were viable and fertile but shorter-lived than the isogenic controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The synaptic neuropil was strongly labeled throughout the brains of larvae and adults with Drep-2C-Term antibody.
source: Subsequently, we used the Drep-2C−Term antibody for wholemount immunostainings of Drosophila brains. The synaptic neuropil was strongly labeled throughout the brains of larvae (not shown) and adults (Figure 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2.

claim: In both drep-2 mutants, Drep-2C−Term staining in the CNS was completely abolished.
source: In both drep-2 mutants, Drep-2C−Term staining in the CNS was completely abolished (drep-2ex13: Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: Drep-2 has been suggested to be involved in the apoptotic regulation of DNA degradation.
source: As a Dff family member, Drep-2 has been suggested to be involved in the apoptotic regulation of DNA degradation (Inohara and Nuñez, 1999; Park and Park, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Inohara and Nuñez, 1999 and Park and Park, 2012.

claim: Neuronal cell bodies lacked Drep-2C−Term staining.
source: However, neuronal cell bodies lacked Drep-2C−Term staining (Figure 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2.

claim: Drep-2 was strongly enriched in fractions containing synaptic membranes.
source: Drep-2 was strongly enriched in fractions containing synaptic membranes (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A.

claim: No enrichment of Drep-2 could be observed in the nuclear fraction.
source: By contrast, no enrichment of Drep-2 could be observed in the nuclear fraction.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Mutants lacking drep-2 showed normal exterior morphology, including their facet eyes.
source: Mutants lacking drep-2 showed normal exterior morphology, including their facet eyes (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Fly facet eyes are highly ordered structures, already displaying abnormal patterns in cases of moderate misregulation of apoptosis.
source: Fly facet eyes are highly ordered structures, already displaying abnormal patterns in cases of moderate misregulation of apoptosis (Wolff and Ready, 1991; Song et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wolff and Ready, 1991 and Song et al., 2000.

claim: The regular facet eyes of drep-2 mutants argue against a major function of the protein in apoptosis.
source: The regular facet eyes of drep-2 mutants, therefore, argue against a major function of the protein in apoptosis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the normal eye morphology shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Wholemount brain stainings of wildtypes and drep-2ex13 mutants showed no apparent morphological differences between either genotype.
source: Wholemount brain stainings of wildtypes and drep-2ex13 mutants also showed no apparent morphological differences between either genotype (Figure 2A,B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2A,B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Drep-2 staining was especially prominent at KC synapses in the mushroom body (MB) calyx of wildtypes.
source: Drep-2 staining was especially prominent at KC synapses in the mushroom body (MB) calyx of wildtypes (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2C.

claim: No differences in the numbers of cell bodies of a subset of MB-intrinsic neurons (KCs) could be observed between drep-2 mutants and controls.
source: We, therefore, quantified the numbers of cell bodies of a subset of MB-intrinsic neurons (KCs). No differences between drep-2 mutants and controls could be observed (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Drep-2 was reported to degrade DNA in vitro.
source: Drep-2 was reported to degrade DNA in vitro (Park and Park, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Park and Park, 2012.

claim: The authors found no evidence of a nuclease activity of Drep-2, even at high concentrations.
source: However, we (Figure 3D) and another previous report (Inohara and Nuñez, 1999) found no evidence of a nuclease activity of Drep-2, even at high concentrations.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3D and supported by citation to Inohara and Nuñez, 1999.

claim: Drep-2 appeared to precipitate DNA.
source: Instead, Drep-2 appeared to precipitate DNA, as evident by plasmid DNA no longer entering the agarose gel when incubated with Drep-2.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The precipitation of DNA by Drep-2 might have generated the previous impression that DNA is degraded in the presence of Drep-2.
source: This precipitation might have generated the previous impression that DNA is degraded in the presence of Drep-2.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data.

claim: The authors could not find evidence for an in vivo role of Drep-2 in regulating apoptosis in the CNS.
source: Taken together, we could not find evidence for an in vivo role of Drep-2 in regulating apoptosis in the CNS.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on multiple lines of evidence presented in the manuscript.

claim: Drep-2C-Term stained synapses throughout the brain, including optic lobes, antennal lobes, and the central complex.
source: While Drep-2C-Term stained synapses throughout the brain, including optic lobes, antennal lobes, and the central complex (Figure 2), the immunoreactivity was particularly pronounced in the MB calyx (Figures 2C and Figure 4A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2.

claim: The immunoreactivity of Drep-2C-Term was particularly pronounced in the MB calyx.
source: While Drep-2C-Term stained synapses throughout the brain, including optic lobes, antennal lobes, and the central complex (Figure 2), the immunoreactivity was particularly pronounced in the MB calyx (Figures 2C and Figure 4A).
evidence: This is shown in Figures 2C and Figure 4A.

claim: The principle circuitry processing olfactory information in Drosophila is highly similar to mammals.
source: The principle circuitry processing olfactory information in Drosophila is highly similar to mammals (Davis, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Davis, 2004.

claim: Signals are transferred in the fly's antennal lobe to projection neurons (PNs), which target the mushroom body (MB) calyx and the lateral protocerebrum.
source: Signals are transferred in the fly's antennal lobe to projection neurons (PNs), which target the mushroom body (MB) calyx and the lateral protocerebrum.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila olfactory circuitry.

claim: PNs synapse in the calyx onto MB-intrinsic Kenyon cells (KCs) by forming large cholinergic presynaptic boutons.
source: PNs synapse in the calyx onto MB-intrinsic Kenyon cells (KCs) by forming large cholinergic presynaptic boutons. These presynaptic specializations are tightly encircled by acetylcholine (ACh) receptor-expressing postsynaptic densities (PSDs) of KC dendritic claws (Yasuyama et al., 2002; Leiss et al., 2009a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yasuyama et al., 2002 and Leiss et al., 2009a.

claim: Presynaptic specializations of PNs are tightly encircled by acetylcholine (ACh) receptor-expressing postsynaptic densities (PSDs) of KC dendritic claws.
source: PNs synapse in the calyx onto MB-intrinsic Kenyon cells (KCs) by forming large cholinergic presynaptic boutons. These presynaptic specializations are tightly encircled by acetylcholine (ACh) receptor-expressing postsynaptic densities (PSDs) of KC dendritic claws (Yasuyama et al., 2002; Leiss et al., 2009a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yasuyama et al., 2002 and Leiss et al., 2009a.

claim: In the MB calyx, the Drep-2C-Term signal overlapped with Dα7 ACh receptor subunits expressed in KC PSDs.
source: In the MB calyx, the Drep-2C-Term signal overlapped with Dα7 ACh receptor subunits expressed in KC PSDs (Figure 4A,B,C′), which surrounded Bruchpilot (Brp)-positive (but Drep-2-negative) PN presynapses (Figure 4A,B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A,B,C′.

claim: Dα7 ACh receptor subunits surrounded Bruchpilot (Brp)-positive (but Drep-2-negative) PN presynapses.
source: In the MB calyx, the Drep-2C-Term signal overlapped with Dα7 ACh receptor subunits expressed in KC PSDs (Figure 4A,B,C′), which surrounded Bruchpilot (Brp)-positive (but Drep-2-negative) PN presynapses (Figure 4A,B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A,B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Drep-2 colocalized with the postsynaptic protein Discs large.
source: Furthermore, Drep-2 colocalized with the postsynaptic protein Discs large, but clearly segregated from presynaptic choline acetyltransferase (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Drep-2 clearly segregated from presynaptic choline acetyltransferase.
source: Furthermore, Drep-2 colocalized with the postsynaptic protein Discs large, but clearly segregated from presynaptic choline acetyltransferase (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Overexpression of UAS-Drep-2mStrawberry with either pan-neural (elavc155-Gal4) or KC-specific drivers (c305a-Gal4) resulted in an mStrawberry signal equivalent to that of the Drep-2C-Term antibody.
source: Consistent with endogenous Drep-2 being present at KC-derived PSDs, overexpression of UAS-Drep-2mStrawberry with either pan-neural (elavc155-Gal4) or KC-specific drivers (c305a-Gal4) resulted in an mStrawberry signal equivalent to that of the Drep-2C-Term antibody (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Overexpression with a PN driver (gh146-Gal4) produced only a weak, diffuse expression pattern that bore no similarity to endogenous Drep-2 staining.
source: Overexpression with a PN driver (gh146-Gal4), however, produced only a weak, diffuse expression pattern that bore no similarity to endogenous Drep-2 staining (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Re-expression of UAS-Drep-2 in KCs of drep-2 mutants produced a distinctive label at KC PSDs.
source: Moreover, re-expression of UAS-Drep-2 in KCs of drep-2 mutants produced a distinctive label at KC PSDs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The presence of Drep-2 at postsynaptic membranes of PN-KC synapses was confirmed by immunoelectron microscopy.
source: Finally, we confirmed the presence of Drep-2 at postsynaptic membranes of PN-KC synapses by immunoelectron microscopy (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Drep-2 accumulates at postsynaptic specializations of KCs within the MB calyx.
source: Thus, Drep-2 accumulates at postsynaptic specializations of KCs within the MB calyx.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on multiple lines of evidence presented in Figures 4.

claim: Kenyon cells have an essential function in olfactory learning.
source: Kenyon cells have an essential function in olfactory learning (Davis, 2011; Dubnau and Chiang, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Davis, 2011 and Dubnau and Chiang, 2013.

claim: In aversive olfactory conditioning, flies are trained to learn the difference between a punished and an unpunished odor.
source: In aversive olfactory conditioning, flies are trained to learn the difference between a punished and an unpunished odor.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental paradigm.

claim: All flies used for behavioral experiments were outcrossed into the isogenic background (w1118) for at least five generations.
source: All flies used for behavioral experiments were outcrossed into our isogenic background (w1118) for at least five generations.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods.

claim: Both mutants drep-2ex13 and drep-2ex27/Dfw45-30n are deficient in aversive olfactory conditioning, 3 min STM in a T-maze.
source: (B) Both mutants drep-2ex13 and drep-2ex27/Dfw45-30n are deficient in aversive olfactory conditioning, 3 min STM in a T-maze.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Re-expression of drep-2 cDNA with elavIII-Gal4 (pan-neural), 30y-Gal4 (MB KCs), or mb247-Gal4 (MB KCs) restores the STM deficit to normal levels.
source: Re-expression of drep-2 cDNA by using either the pan-neural driver elavIII-Gal4 or two different KC-specific drivers (30y-Gal4 and mb247-Gal4) was sufficient to rescue STM scores (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Drep-2 is required in KCs for normal olfactory STM.
source: Drep-2 is, therefore, required in KCs for normal olfactory STM.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the rescue experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: ITM is composed of two memory components, consolidated anesthesia-resistant memory (ARM) and labile anesthesia-sensitive memory (ASM).
source: ITM is composed of two memory components, consolidated anesthesia-resistant memory (ARM) and labile anesthesia-sensitive memory (ASM) (Quinn and Dudai, 1976; Tully et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Quinn and Dudai, 1976 and Tully et al., 1994.

claim: ASM and ARM rely on different molecular and neuronal mechanisms.
source: ASM and ARM rely on different molecular and neuronal mechanisms (Folkers et al., 1993; Tully et al., 1994; Scheunemann et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Folkers et al., 1993; Tully et al., 1994; Scheunemann et al., 2012.

claim: The drep-2 mutants exhibited regular ARM but were deficient in ASM.
source: The drep-2 mutants exhibited regular ARM but were deficient in ASM (Figure 5D), which was evidenced by memory scores not differing between cooled and untreated drep-2 mutants.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5D.

claim: This loss of ASM was rescued by re-expression of drep-2 using elavIII-Gal4 or KC-specific mb247-Gal4.
source: This loss of ASM was rescued by re-expression of drep-2 using elavIII-Gal4 or KC-specific mb247-Gal4.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Drep-2 is required in KCs for both STM and ASM, but not for ARM.
source: We conclude that Drep-2 is required in KCs for both STM and ASM, but not for ARM.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the behavioral data in Figure 5.

claim: Morphologies of drep-2-mutant MBs and PN-KC synapses appeared normal.
source: Concurrently, morphologies of drep-2-mutant MBs and PN-KC synapses appeared normal (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The number of synapses in the MB calyx did not differ between drep-2 mutants and controls.
source: Furthermore, the number of synapses in the MB calyx did not differ between either genotype (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: drep-2-mutant phenotypes should not be caused by gross structural developmental aberrations.
source: Thus, drep-2-mutant phenotypes should not be caused by gross structural developmental aberrations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the normal morphology shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: It appeared likely that Drep-2 might intersect with signaling pathways involved in synaptic plasticity.
source: Instead, given the synaptic localization of the protein, it appeared likely that Drep-2 might intersect with signaling pathways involved in synaptic plasticity.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the synaptic localization and behavioral phenotypes.

claim: PN-KC synapses use ACh as the main fast neurotransmitter.
source: PN-KC synapses, as is the case for many excitatory synapses in the Drosophila CNS, use ACh as the main fast neurotransmitter (Gu and O'Dowd, 2006; Yasuyama et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gu and O'Dowd, 2006 and Yasuyama et al., 2002.

claim: Drep-2 colocalized with nicotinic ACh receptor subunits at PN-KC synapses.
source: Drep-2 colocalized here with nicotinic ACh receptor subunits (Figure 4).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4.

claim: Several types of metabotropic receptor are expressed in the calyx, including GABAB, dopamine, octopamine, and metabotropic glutamate receptors.
source: In addition, several types of metabotropic receptor are also expressed in the calyx, including GABAB, dopamine, octopamine, and metabotropic glutamate receptors (Enell et al., 2007; Devaud et al., 2008; Busch et al., 2009; Mao and Davis, 2009; Kanellopoulos et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Enell et al., 2007; Devaud et al., 2008; Busch et al., 2009; Mao and Davis, 2009; Kanellopoulos et al., 2012.

claim: DmGluRA is the single functional metabotropic glutamate receptor (mGluR) in Drosophila.
source: DmGluRA is the single functional metabotropic glutamate receptor (mGluR) in Drosophila (Parmentier et al., 1996), orthologous to mammalian group II/III mGluRs.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Parmentier et al., 1996.

claim: DmGluRA is orthologous to mammalian group II/III mGluRs.
source: DmGluRA is the single functional metabotropic glutamate receptor (mGluR) in Drosophila (Parmentier et al., 1996), orthologous to mammalian group II/III mGluRs.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Parmentier et al., 1996.

claim: DmGluRA and the mGluR-associated protein Homer show a characteristic expression throughout the Drosophila brain, with strong expression in the MB calyx.
source: DmGluRA and the mGluR-associated protein Homer show a characteristic expression throughout the Drosophila brain, with strong expression in the MB calyx (Ramaekers et al., 2001; Diagana et al., 2002; Hamasaka et al., 2007; Urizar et al., 2007; Devaud et al., 2008; Kahsai et al., 2012; Kanellopoulos et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ramaekers et al., 2001; Diagana et al., 2002; Hamasaka et al., 2007; Urizar et al., 2007; Devaud et al., 2008; Kahsai et al., 2012; Kanellopoulos et al., 2012.

claim: Drep-2 colocalized with both mGluR and Homer throughout the brain.
source: We examined different receptor types and related proteins for colocalization with Drep-2 (not shown). Drep-2 colocalized with both mGluR and Homer throughout the brain (not shown), with very prominent co-labeling in the MB calyx (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Drep-2 showed very prominent co-labeling with mGluR and Homer in the MB calyx.
source: We examined different receptor types and related proteins for colocalization with Drep-2 (not shown). Drep-2 colocalized with both mGluR and Homer throughout the brain (not shown), with very prominent co-labeling in the MB calyx (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6A.

claim: mGluR signaling is a prime candidate for a pathway interacting with Drep-2 function.
source: This made mGluR signaling a prime candidate for a pathway interacting with Drep-2 function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the colocalization data.

claim: mGluRs have been found to be important for olfactory conditioning in flies.
